name: Chafing Dishes
tagline: Heat that holds, hinges that stay quiet.
intro: The centrepiece of every buffet line and the hardest-working piece in the room. Ours are built around the failure points — the hinge, the fuel holder, the food-pan seat — because that is where a chafer dies first.
buyer_note: Specify by pan size (GN 1/1 or 2/3), fuel type and lid action. Roll-top for a long line where staff pass in one direction; lift-off for tight corners.

name: Wine Coolers & Ice Buckets
tagline: Cold held long enough to matter.
intro: Double-walled where it counts, weighted at the base so a bottle cannot tip it, and finished on the inside as carefully as the outside — because in a wine cooler the inside is what the guest sees.
buyer_note: Double-wall holds temperature roughly twice as long as single-wall and never sweats onto linen. For banquet volume, ask about the stand-mounted party tub.

name: Trays & Platters
tagline: Balanced in the hand before it is beautiful on the table.
intro: A tray is judged by a server carrying it one-handed across a full room. We set the handle height and the rim angle for that, then hammer the face for the light.
buyer_note: Hand-hammered faces hide scuffing far better than mirror-polished ones — the single most useful thing to know when buying for daily service.

name: Charger Plates
intro: A charger never holds food; it holds attention. Thirteen inches of worked metal under a white dinner plate is the cheapest way a banquet hall can look twice its price.
buyer_note: Order in multiples of your table count plus 10% for rotation and repair. Ask for the rim profile that suits your plate diameter — a 13" charger under a 12" plate leaves no reveal.

name: Serveware & Bowls
tagline: For the food that arrives at the table, not the buffet.
intro: Handis, gravy boats, salad bowls, dessert stands. The pieces that leave the kitchen full and come back empty, several times a night.
buyer_note: Insulated double-wall bowls keep a salad crisp through a two-hour brunch and never ring with condensation on the tablecloth.

name: Buffet Stands & Risers
tagline: Height is what makes a buffet look designed.
intro: A flat buffet reads as a canteen. Three heights and a cloche read as a hotel. These are the pieces that do that work.
buyer_note: Buy risers as a set of graduated heights rather than singly — the proportion between them is the whole effect.

name: Barware & Accessories
tagline: The small metal on the bar and the table.
intro: Shakers, pitchers, napkin rings, menu holders. Individually minor, collectively the difference between a room that was furnished and a room that was styled.
buyer_note: This is the category to use for branding — a logo embossed on a napkin ring or a menu holder costs little and is seen at every cover.
